text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
FRONT PAGE POLITICAL NEWS
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Over 170,000 supporters of Solidarity's constitution proposal have signed a petition demanding that the bill should also be presented at the coming constitutional referundum in May this year, the right-wing nationalist Movement for the Reconstruction of Poland (ROP) said.
- Around 51 percent of Poles have criticised the recent decision to liquidate the Gdansk shipyard and 28 percent say it was the right thing to do, a PBS polling agency survey said.
NOWA EUROPA

- Polish Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz will discuss the recent dismissal of Agriculture Minister Roman Jagielinski with political leaders of the co-ruling Polish Peasants Party (PSL) this week.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET NEWS
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Investments by Poland's corporate sector grew by 26 percent compared with the year before, which showed the biggest growth since market reforms began in 1989, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.

- The European Union has recently adopted a uniform system of veterinary regulations which will result in the ban of U.S.-produced chicken imports to Europe, as new EU hygienic norms are not met in the production process.
Russia is expected to adopt the new system as well, which may open its market to Polish poultry producers.
- Japan's Toyota car maker is considering new plant construction in Poland, Toyota Motor Poland director Adam Kolodziejczyk said.
The concern is now producing a feasibility study on its new Europe-located plant construction scheme.
It is too early to give any specific information on the the factory's location now, Toyota Motor Europe spokeswoman Brigitte Delvenne said.
- The Polish Ocean Lines (PLO) made a net profit last year and carried out development investments for the first time in seven years, PLO court appointed manager Miroslaw Hapko said.
The company has contracted four second-hand vessels and will lease them this year to its Pol-America subsidiary.
PLO is now operating 44 vessels.
- The Kapena bus maker in Slupsk has developed a new bus model with a capacity of 30 passengers.
The new fuel-economic bus, which is adapted to urban transportation needs, will be exhibited at the Poznan international fair in April.
- Germany's AN Nutfahrzeuge bus maker will invest 25 million marks in new plant construction in Tarnow Podgorny, western Poland, through its MAN Pojazdy Uzytkowe Polska subsidiary.
Initially, the plant's annual output will be 120 buses, the subsidiary company said.

- Insufficient component deliveries from the German Volkswagen (VW) factory in Wolfsburg to the VW Poznan plant will cause delays in handing over the VW Polo cars contracted in Poland, Kulczyk Tradex representative Piotr Chyrek said.
NOWA EUROPA
- Telekomunikacja Polska SA (TPSA), the state-owned telecoms monopolist, has already launched Internet servers in 25 provinces around Poland.
By the end of 1997 all TPSA subscribers will have Internet access, the company said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- Four Polish insurance firms: TUK, PZU, Warta and Partner have slashed prices of "green card" insurance policies for drivers abroad, the comapnies said.
ZYCIE
- France's Castorama supermarket chain has opened its first supermarket in Poland. The chain plans to open 16 supermarkets around the country by 2002.
PARKIET
- Listed leather-goods maker Chemiskor's net profit in March will grow by 800,000 zlotys as the result of a land parcel sale.
Chemiskor's net profit for all of 1996 was 640,000 zlotys.

- The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) is considering buying a stake in the listed Stalexport steel producer and trader worth up to $30 million, Stalexport's president Ryszard Harhala said.
-- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
